s: are_brought_to Emerald City [to Ozma's palace] Ozma has the marble statues of Unc Nunkie and Margolotte brought to the Emerald City palace. She says they are standing in the next room and leads the party toward them.

l: luck, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
s: is_associated_with number thirteen [according to the Tin Woodman] The Tin Woodman tells Ojo that Friday, the number thirteen, being left-handed, and having a wart are not signs of bad luck. He urges Ojo to call himself Ojo the Lucky and says that people who fear bad luck may fail to notice good fortune.

l: the statue of Unc Nunkie, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
s: depicts Unc Nunkie [before restoration] The statue of Unc Nunkie stands in the room until the Wonderful Wizard of Oz makes a magic pass and speaks a magic word before it. Unc Nunkie immediately comes to life.

l: the statue of Margolotte, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
s: depicts Margolotte [before restoration] The statue of Margolotte is present in the room until the Wonderful Wizard of Oz makes a magic pass and speaks a magic word before it. Margolotte then moves, comes to life, and runs to Dr. Pipt.

l: the nice house outside the Emerald City, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
s: Ozma gives the nice house outside the Emerald City to Ojo and Unc Nunkie as their future home. They will live there under her protection.

l: Sky Island
s: Sky Island is L. Frank Baum’s fairyland adventure about Trot, Cap’n Bill, and Button-Bright, continuing Trot and Cap’n Bill’s earlier adventures. Button-Bright arrives beside the Pacific Ocean from Philadelphia after traveling by his family’s Magic Umbrella, which flies to any named destination but cannot be redirected or stopped. Trot, Button-Bright, and Cap’n Bill test it, then fly toward Sky Island and become stranded there when the umbrella is seized. On the Blue side of the island, the travelers are captured by Quitey Righty Boolooroo, ruler of the Blueskins. Trot is made servant to the Six Snubnosed Princesses, Cap’n Bill is assigned as Royal Nectar Mixer, and Button-Bright as Royal Bootblue. With help from Ghip-Ghisizzle, who believes the Boolooroo has illegally prolonged his rule by hiding the Royal Record Book, they seek the umbrella. Button-Bright retrieves the Record Book but not the umbrella, and the three escape through the Great Fog Bank into the sunny Pink Country. The Pinkies treat them more comfortably but debate whether outsiders must be thrown from Sky Island. Rosalie the Witch confirms their story yet supports expelling them. At the island’s edge, Polychrome, the Rainbow’s Daughter, arrives and interprets the laws to make Trot the rightful Queen of the Pink Country. Trot, Cap’n Bill, and Button-Bright resolve to recover the umbrella, while Rosalie proposes an army to confront the Boolooroo. Cap’n Bill commands the Pinkies’ march through the fog against the Blues. During the conflict he is captured, and Trot uses Rosalie’s invisibility ring to enter the Blue City. She disrupts the planned patching punishment, helps Ghip-Ghisizzle escape, and ultimately saves Cap’n Bill. The Boolooroo is defeated by the very punishment intended for Cap’n Bill, aided by Trot and a billygoat. Trot takes control of both countries, ends the war, makes Ghip-Ghisizzle the new Boolooroo, banishes the former Boolooroo and the Princesses, and destroys the Great Knife. After finding the umbrella on a rubbish heap, the party returns through the Fog Bank, where the umbrella briefly becomes an elephant. Trot reforms Pink Country rule, appoints Rosalie Queen, and then flies home with Cap’n Bill and Button-Bright. Button-Bright safely reaches Philadelphia, and his father locks the Magic Umbrella away.

l: Sky Island, Sky Island
s: Sky Island is an English eBook by L. Frank Baum, the second story in the adventures of Trot and Cap'n Bill. Available through Project Gutenberg as eBook 4356, it was released August 1, 2003, and updated December 27, 2020. Baum introduces it as his present story, centered on Button-Bright and his Magic Umbrella, and invites readers' responses.

l: Project Gutenberg, Sky Island
s: publishes Sky Island [as an eBook] Project Gutenberg distributes Sky Island for use at no cost and with almost no restrictions in the United States and most other parts of the world. It provides the Project Gutenberg License and advises users outside the United States to check the laws of their own countries.

l: L. Frank Baum, Sky Island
s: L. Frank Baum is identified as Sky Island’s author and writes its introductory talk, linking it with The Sea Fairies and earlier characters while inviting children to write to him at Ozcot in Hollywood, California.

l: Sky Island, Sky Island
s: Sky Island is a book, following Trot and Cap'n Bill's visit to The Sea Fairies, and is dedicated to Mary Louise Brewster. Its story begins when Trot, Cap'n Bill, and Button-Bright are carried by the Magic Umbrella toward an island suspended in the sky. The island is surrounded by sky rather than water; its edges are guarded in places by bushes or fences because anyone who steps beyond them tumbles away. It has trees, ponds, houses, and three countries: the Blue Country, the Fog Country, and the Pink Country. The travelers first reach the blue part, where gardens, buildings, vegetation, paths, and water are blue. The Blue Country is ruled by the Boolooroo, whose palace adjoins their landing place. Though he calls the government a republic, he directs elections and punishes disobedience. He and his court call Sky Island the Center of the Universe. The island is a fairy country whose people do not visibly age and cannot die before six hundred years. The Great Fog Bank separates the equal-sized Blue and Pink Countries. Trot and her companions, initially seeking to escape, become involved in the conflicts of both lands. The narrative proceeds through the Pink Country, its queens and tribes, the arrival of Polychrome, war between Pinks and Blues, Cap'n Bill's capture, Trot's invisible adventure, and the conquest of the Blues. After victory, Trot becomes Queen of Sky Island except the Fog Bank, while the Blue and Pink Countries retain separate rulers. Before leaving, she regulates the Pinkies by leaving Rosalie to rule the Pink Country. Trot, Cap'n Bill, and Button-Bright then say goodbye to their friends and fly upward from Sky Island in the Magic Umbrella to return home.

l: Trot, Sky Island
s: Trot is a little girl from Earth, the daughter of Mrs. Griffith and Cap'n Griffith, who lives in a frame cottage and is Cap'n Bill's close companion and friend. She meets Button-Bright near the Pacific Ocean, believes his account of the Magic Umbrella, and eagerly joins him and Cap'n Bill on an air-ride intended for a picnic. The umbrella instead carries them to Sky Island. There Trot repeatedly resists unjust treatment. In the Blue Country, the Boolooroo imprisons the travelers, and the Six Snubnosed Princesses seize Trot as their maid and slave. Though shaken and slapped, she refuses inwardly to accept slavery, wins the protection of the princesses' pets, reunites with her companions, and escapes through the Fog Bank. In the Pink Country, she and her friends face possible expulsion, but Polychrome identifies Trot as the lightest-skinned person present, making her Queen under the country's succession law. Trot accepts the Pinkies' support while keeping return to Earth and recovery of the Magic Umbrella as central goals. When Cap'n Bill is captured, she uses Rosalie's ring to enter the Blue City invisibly, frees Tiggle, searches the palace, and repeatedly risks herself to rescue Cap'n Bill. She uses a rope to save him from the Great Knife, helps overthrow the Boolooroo, and ends patching and the Great Knife's threat. After the victory, Trot rules the Pink and Blue Countries as Queen of Sky Island, appointing Cap'n Bill and later Ghip-Ghisizzle to govern the Blues, protecting the Pinkies, and banishing the former Boolooroo and the princesses. She delays departure until she has arranged affairs responsibly. Back in the Pink Country, she makes a law granting the Queen equal conditions, appoints Rosalie Queen, orders a palace and statues, and then returns home with Cap'n Bill and Button-Bright in the Magic Umbrella.

l: Cap'n Bill, Sky Island
s: Cap'n Bill is an old, retired, one-legged sailor from Earth who lives with Trot and her mother. Friendly, cheerful, honest, knowledgeable, and meek, he is Trot's close chum and devoted protector, caring for her exceptionally well. Though skeptical of Button-Bright's Magic Umbrella, he builds seats for it, joins Trot and Button-Bright on its flight, and becomes both frightened and resourceful when they reach Sky Island. Captured by the Boolooroo of the Blues, Cap'n Bill is made a palace slave and Royal Nectar Mixer. He explores the Blue City, escapes with Trot and Button-Bright, and endures the Fog Bank before the group reaches the Pink Country. There he favors the Pinkies over the Blues, supports Trot after she becomes Queen, and urges a campaign to recover the Magic Umbrella and confront the Boolooroo. As Commander in Chief of Trot's Army of Conquest, he leads the Pinkies through the Fog Bank and against the Blue City. During the fighting he directs the Pinkies but is captured after falling when his wooden leg enters a hole. The Boolooroo plans to patch him to Tiggle, but Trot repeatedly saves him from the Great Knife and frees him. He then helps bind the Boolooroo, supports Trot's rule, and becomes her General and Royal Manager of the Blue Country. After the victory, Cap'n Bill helps find the discarded umbrella, seats, and lunch basket. He travels back through the Fog Bank, prepares the equipment, pilots the return journey with Trot and Button-Bright, and regards getting back to Earth as the best part of the adventure.

l: Magic Umbrella, Sky Island
s: Magic Umbrella is an old, large, strong but disreputable-looking family relic, handed down through Button-Bright's family. Its thick brown cloth has faded to dull drab, and its wooden handle is carved as an elephant's head with red-stone eyes and tiny ivory tusks. It has ropes, two wooden seats, and a wicker basket or lunch-basket attached, allowing it to carry as many as three passengers. Found by Button-Bright in his attic, it is magical through fairy enchantment rather than power of its own. When Button-Bright or another rightful family member holds it open and speaks a destination, it flies rapidly and safely there, obeying the destination but neither stopping nor changing course beforehand. It cannot grant wishes for ice-cream soda or money, and it refuses to return early when Button-Bright changes his mind. It carries Button-Bright, Trot, and Cap'n Bill on journeys over land, ocean, clouds, and an arched path through the heavens, including travel to Sky Island and the Blue Country. On Sky Island, the Boolooroo repeatedly takes the umbrella to prevent the travelers' escape. Though it belongs to Button-Bright's family and will not work for the Boolooroo, he has it carried to the Royal Treasury, tests it, and throws it beneath a cabinet. It disappears from the Treasure Chamber and remains missing despite extensive searches. Eventually Tiggle recalls throwing it from beneath the cabinet onto a rubbish heap, where Cap'n Bill finds it and Button-Bright recovers it. When rejected by the Frog King, it transforms into a huge elephant, leads the travelers through the Fog Bank, and becomes an umbrella again at the Pink Country's edge. Finally, commanded to take the travelers to Trot's house, it carries Trot, Cap'n Bill, and Button-Bright safely from Sky Island to Earth. Button-Bright later flies to Philadelphia with it, after which his father locks it in a strong chest in the attic.

l: Blue City, Sky Island
s: Blue City is a blue city in Blue Country, inhabited by Blueskins and extending a half mile in every direction from its center. Broad blue-marble streets run among blue buildings, castles, shops, spires, and turrets. It contains the Royal Palace, the Boolooroo's palace, and the Room of the Great Knife; its city wall surrounds it, connects with the palace-garden wall, and has a principal gate. Outer walls protect it against the country beyond. At first, Button-Bright and Cap'n Bill tour the city with Ghip-Ghisizzle. Later, fugitives find it deserted, but an alarm brings lights, shouts, angry citizens, guards, and pursuers. As the Pinkies approach, Blueskins rush inside, the Boolooroo closes and locks the gates, and Cap'n Bill's army halts outside the wall. The Blueskins capture Cap'n Bill within the city, while Trot secretly climbs over the wall. At night the city is quiet and blue-lit but joins the pursuit of Ghip-Ghisizzle; finally it wakes as Cap'n Bill tries to escape and soldiers pursue him along the wall, while Ghip-Ghisizzle plans an attack on it.

l: the Pink Country, Sky Island
s: The Pink Country, also called the Sunset Country, is a pink country forming one half of Sky Island, separated from the Blue Country by the Fog Bank. About two square miles in area, it borders the fog and has a dangerous outer edge dropping into the gulf below. It is a land of sunrises and sunsets, with pink grass, trees, paths, sky, clouds, sunlight, marble public spaces, and round buildings without corners or angles; its neat, garden-like landscape ranges from faint rose to deep pink. It contains the City and Tourmaline's palace, and is inhabited by several hundred Pinkies, including the eastern Sunrise Tribe and western Sunset Tribe. Its prosperity, color uniformity, and laws matter greatly. Under Tourmaline, the Pinkies initially have no established place for outsiders and consider expelling Trot, Button-Bright, and Cap'n Bill after they emerge from the Fog Bank. Polychrome interprets the laws to protect the travelers and make Trot Queen. Tourmaline is relieved, Trot is received as the new Queen, and the customs require a poor plain dress and little pleasure. After Trot and her companions return from the Blue Country, the country welcomes them; Trot leaves Rosalie the Witch to rule under the new law.

l: the Boolooroo, Sky Island
s: The Boolooroo, Quitey Righty, is the sky-blue king and elected monarch of Sky Island, also called the Blue Country and the country of the Blueskins. He has a round body and long neck, blue skin, eyes, hair, and clothing, and wears a star-shaped jewel with blue stones. Though elected for a three-hundred-year term, he claims to have reigned not quite two hundred years; the Royal Book of Records shows that he has completed, and exceeded, his lawful term. He keeps that book and the Royal Treasury locked up, with the key in his pocket, apparently to conceal his fraud and retain power. What matters most is his cruel, deceitful rule. He steals Button-Bright's Magic Umbrella, enslaves Trot, Cap'n Bill, and Button-Bright, and assigns them work in Sky Island. He threatens punishment by “patching,” a punishment he invented, and uses the Great Knife against prisoners. He is feared, hated, and friendless; he hates everyone, treats the strangers cruelly, and is afraid of the Pinkies. He is father of the Six Snubnosed Princesses and married to the Queen, but even his household brings him anger and demands. As the travelers seek escape and the Book of Records threatens his position, he suspects Ghip-Ghisizzle, orders him bound and scheduled for patching, and tries to hold his rule during the Pinkies' invasion. He imprisons Cap'n Bill and repeatedly orders him patched, eventually proposing to join him to a billygoat. When he tries to operate the Great Knife, the goat knocks him down, and Trot and Cap'n Bill bind him beneath it. Trot takes control, keeps him locked in the Room of the Great Knife, and removes him from rule because he has ruled beyond his lawful term. He loses the palace and treasure and must leave with the Six Snubnosed Princesses, saying he will reform and become a model private citizen.

l: the Blueskins, Sky Island
s: The Blueskins are blue, long-legged people of the Blue City and soldiers of the Boolooroo, serving under the Captain of the Guards. Their only arms are cords until they use bluewood lances. They attack the Pinkies, retreat from sharp sticks, are defeated by enchanted weapons, and capture Cap'n Bill. After returning cautiously, they obey Trot, imprison the princesses, and prepare the Blue City for the Pinkies' arrival.

l: the Six Snubnosed Princesses, Sky Island
s: The Six Snubnosed Princesses are six sister princesses of Sky Island, daughters of the Boolooroo and Queen, and royal daughters of the Revered and Resplendent Royal Ruler of the Blues. They are gorgeously dressed Blueskin girls with blue gowns and hair, huge towers of hair, long thin necks, and snub noses regarded as high breeding. Haughty, cruel, and vindictive, they habitually mistreat their favored animal and bird pets. They claim Trot as their maid, slave, and living pincushion, fasten six ribbons to her, and drag her into the Blue Palace, where they order her to serve them and seek harsh punishment for her after their pets rebel. They also quarrel over marrying Ghip-Ghisizzle to become Queen, free him from the Room of the Great Knife, and confine him until he chooses one of them. When the billygoat attacks during Cap'n Bill's patching, they are thrown into the corridor in terror. Later they reject Trot's rule and each demands the kingdom, but Trot has them locked under guard, making them meek and mild. After Trot's victory, they and their parents are expelled from the palace and escorted, screaming and hysterical, to Ghip-Ghisizzle's small cabin.

l: Ghip-Ghisizzle, Sky Island
s: Ghip-Ghisizzle is a Blueskin royal officer, Majordomo, and Master of Ceremonies in the Blue Country, marked by a blue-gold chain and expected to become the Boolooroo. He is friendly and protective toward Button-Bright, Cap'n Bill, Trot, and the other strangers, guiding them through the Blue City, explaining its customs, giving them rooms, and trying to shield them from hostile servants, soldiers, and the Boolooroo's plan to send them through the Arch of Phinis. He sympathizes with the prisoners because he disapproves of their treatment. His central concern is the succession. Though the current Boolooroo dislikes him and conceals the length of his reign, Ghip-Ghisizzle believes the Royal Record Book can establish whether he is the lawful ruler. After the Book disappears, he denies taking it and suspects Button-Bright. The Boolooroo has him bound and schedules him to be patched with Tiggle. The Six Snubnosed Princesses rescue him only to confine him and demand that he marry one of them; he refuses. He escapes over the City Wall, reaches the Pinkies' camp, and is captured by Captain Coralie. With the Royal Record Book, Ghip-Ghisizzle learns that the Boolooroo has ruled beyond the lawful three hundred years and that he has been the rightful ruler since Thursday. He seeks the former Boolooroo's resignation and agrees to help Button-Bright and the Pinkies recover the Magic Umbrella if they help him. Trot appoints him Boolooroo, and he becomes ruler of the Blue Country. He opposes patching, agrees to destroy the Great Knife and care for the billygoat, offers his little cabin to the former royal family, refuses to marry the former Princesses because he judges them wicked, and is ordered by Trot to treat the people of the Blue City nicely while she is away.

l: Button-Bright, Sky Island
s: Button-Bright is a boy from Philadelphia, an Earth person whose formal name is Saladin Paracelsus de Lambertine Evagne von Smith. He is a descendant and member of the family that rightfully owns the old Magic Umbrella, a precious family relic with an elephant-head handle. After finding it in an attic, he discovers that it can carry him through the air and flies from Philadelphia across several places to the Pacific Ocean, arriving by parachute-like descent and meeting Trot and Cap'n Bill. Though he says he dislikes most girls and boys, he considers Trot one of the good ones and becomes her companion. The umbrella matters most to Button-Bright: it enables the journey, is repeatedly lost or sought, and is his means of returning home. He directs it toward Sky Island, but its literal obedience brings the travelers into danger. In the Blue Country, the Boolooroo takes the umbrella, enslaves Button-Bright, and makes him Royal Bootblue, responsible for blueing and shining royal footwear. Button-Bright plans an escape, steals the Treasure Chamber key, enters the chamber despite the Blue Wolf, fails to find the umbrella, and escapes with the Royal Record Book concealed in his blouse. With Trot, Cap'n Bill, and later the parrot, he crosses the Fog Bank into the Pink Country. He tells their story, fears their uncertain fate, wants to return to Earth, and recognizes Polychrome as an old friend when she helps save them. During the conflict with the Boolooroo, he leads the Pinkies, supports Ghip-Ghisizzle if he will rule, and makes return of the Magic Umbrella a condition of his help. The Royal Record Book establishes that the Boolooroo has completed his lawful reign. After the victory, Button-Bright searches for and recovers the umbrella, carries it through its brief transformation involving its elephant head, and finally travels with Trot and Cap'n Bill back to Earth. He stays at Trot's house, flies home to Philadelphia, and reports that he arrived safely.

l: the Blue Wolf, Sky Island
s: The Blue Wolf is a monstrous, ravenous animal in the Blue City, terrible and fearful in aspect, with a lion-sized head, powerful shoulders and front legs, flashing blue eyes, and needle-sharp foot-long teeth. Crouching near the Treasure Chamber entrance, it guards the Royal Treasure Chamber. It attacks Button-Bright, who jams a sofa pillow in its jaws; the wolf cannot free its teeth and struggles to remove it with its claws.

l: Fog Bank, Sky Island
s: Fog Bank is a thick, heavy, blue-grey fog bank across the center of the island, between the Blue Country and the Pink Country. It is an impassable-seeming barrier around the Blue Country: blinding, wet, clinging, sticky, and unhealthy for humans to remain in. Its dampness soaks clothes and hair, and those who enter are said to lose their six hundred allowed years and become liable to die at any time. Yet its pebbled ground can be seen, and it is the Paradise of Frogs, home to common frogs and giant frogs. It has no parsnips. It first separates the Blue Country from the Pink Country and from the travelers' approach. Button-Bright, Cap'n Bill, Trot, and the blue parrot plunge into it to escape the Blueskins, who will not follow. A common frog guides them through its moist gray mist; near the Pink Country it turns soft rose, and they eventually emerge soaked, chilled, and with wrinkled, discolored clothing. Later, with a big frog, they escape through it again. Though a law sends Blueskins who break through it back with sharp sticks, it does not apply to the strangers. The Pinkies later cross it in about a dozen jumps with giant frogs and enter the Blue Country. Ghip-Ghisizzle fears Button-Bright may be lost in it. The fog remains the only part of Sky Island outside Trot's kingdom. It is crossed again with frogs and under the transformed elephant's guidance; its pink glow continues to signal the Pink Country. Trot and her companions plan to dive into it when leaving for the Land of Sunrise and Sunset.

l: Tourmaline, Sky Island
s: Tourmaline is the young, beautiful, light-pink Queen of the Pinkies and sole ruler of the Pink Country. About seventeen, slender and rosy-complexioned, she wears a plain coarse pink robe and a rose-gold brow band bearing a luminous pink jewel. Though her word is law and she holds absolute authority, including the power to enforce laws and decree death when punishment is merited, she is modest, plain, and poor by principle. Living in a plain stone palace, she darns her own stockings and believes a ruler should be a public servant, not rich or falsely admired. As queen, Tourmaline consults the Great Book of Laws when strangers arrive, convenes the twelve Counselors, and seeks a decision on whether the travelers should remain as guests or be thrown over the island’s edge. When the Council divides evenly, she will not cast the deciding vote because she finds it impolite to oppose Counselors, instead asking Rosalie the Witch to decide. She orders the strangers cast away because they do not harmonize with the Pink Country’s color scheme, pressing for immediate execution even in rain. Later, she accepts Polychrome’s reading of the protection law and yields her circlet when Trot is identified as the rightful Queen. After losing the throne, Tourmaline appears in fine robes but declines restoration, saying queenship brought want and misery and that she prefers freedom. Trot orders a pink marble statue of her placed in the Court of the Statues after her death.

l: Poverty Queen, Sky Island
s: Poverty Queen is Trot’s regulation of the Queen of the Pinkies: she receives the same food, dresses, good times, housing, and spending money as the people, cannot take more, and faces being pushed off the edge if she does.

l: the Sunrise Tribe, Sky Island
s: The Sunrise Tribe occupies the eastern half of the Pink Country, claims importance because the sun greets it first, lives at peace with the Sunset Tribe, and has six members on Tourmaline’s Council questioning strangers’ fit.

l: Sunset Tribe, Sky Island
s: The Sunset Tribe occupies the western half of the Pink Country, claims importance because the sun reaches it after leaving the Sunrise Tribe, gathers nightly to watch sunset, and has six Council members including its leader, Coralie.

l: Rosalie the Witch, Sky Island
s: Rosalie the Witch is a famous, wise, honest, rosy-pink witch, somewhat taller than most Pinkies, with a slender staff tipped by a lustrous pink jewel. Though not very obliging and prone to headaches from witchcraft, she has useful but limited powers: only one magic charm every three days. She has no power over frogs, keeps Ghip-Ghisizzle prisoner in her tent, and is friends with giant frogs. Summoned as the wise and honest deciding voter, she uses a vision to confirm the Earth people's account, votes to throw them from the island, and expects fairies to protect them through the Magic Umbrella. She advises the Army of Conquest's size, secures the frogs' help across the Fog Bank, sees events in the Blue City, enchants the Pinkies' sticks, and helps the rescue effort with a rope ladder and the invisibility ring she lends Trot. After victory, she urges the group to return before conflict between Pinkies and Blueskins. She refuses queenship under an old law that would make its ruler poor and miserable, but after Trot changes it, accepts appointment as Queen of the Pinkies. Loved and respected, she rules and protects them, cares for a parrot given by Trot, and remains on Sky Island with Coralie and Tourmaline when Trot leaves because they have no Magic Umbrella.

l: Rosalie the Witch, Sky Island
s: Rosalie the Witch pledges to protect and serve Trot while Trot rules the Pink Country, proposing to lead the Pinkies through the Fog Bank against the Boolooroo to recover the Magic Umbrella and assist the campaign.

l: Polychrome, Sky Island
s: Polychrome is the Rainbow's Daughter, a fairy of the sky who lives in sky country and has powers far stronger than Rosalie the Witch's. She arrives by descending from the Rainbow to aid her old friend Button-Bright and the travelers, protecting Trot from threatened execution. Challenging Tourmaline, she interprets the Great Book of Laws in the travelers' favor, makes Trot Queen by placing Tourmaline's circlet on her, and leads her before the Pinkies. After asking Rosalie to protect Trot and promising to watch over Button-Bright, Polychrome leaves with her sisters on the Rainbow.

l: Queen Mayre, Sky Island
s: is_a queen Mayre is named in the contents as Queen of the Pink Country.

l: Queen of the Pink Country, Sky Island
s: The Queen of the Pinkies is an office regulated by Trot under a new law: its holder has the same food, dresses, good times, money, and no better home than the people. Trot holds it temporarily, then appoints Rosalie the Witch.

l: the Pinkies, Sky Island
s: The Pinkies are the several hundred short, round, chubby, wholly pink people of Pink Country, with pink hair, eyes, cheeks, complexions, clothing, and a pink color scheme. Wealthy, polite, strong, and devoted to their laws, they regard wealth and honor as their due. Their society includes the Sunrise and Sunset Tribes, treats women as important as men in work and war, and uses long sharp-pointed sticks as weapons. They are ruled first by Tourmaline, whom they acknowledge as Queen, and regard the Blueskins as natural enemies. At first suspicious of outsiders, Pinkies capture and escort the travelers to Tourmaline, fearing enemies, magicians, or sorcerers. Although they do not hate the strangers, they have never admitted outsiders and support an order to execute them. Rosalie's explanation and Polychrome's interpretation of the laws change their response: they kneel to Trot, recognize her as Queen, and spread news of her rule. Eager for relief from monotonous lives, they form a two-hundred-warrior army and invade Blue Country across the Fog Bank on giant frogs. They camp outside Blue City, repel an attack, and, after Rosalie enchants their sticks, destroy the Blueskins' longer lances. They suffer setbacks in attempts to save Cap'n Bill, capture Ghip-Ghisizzle, and prepare to assault the City. Instead, Trot orders peace and they enter Blue City as welcomed conquerors. They celebrate but refuse to dance with the Blues and quarrel with them. Anxious to return home, the Pinkies travel back through the Fog Bank. They welcome Trot's return, accept her new law granting the Queen equal conditions as just, accept Rosalie as Queen, and promise her a palace and statues. They give Trot the royal pink-gold band with its pink jewel. At the end, their Pink Band plays while they gather in the Court of the Statues to bid Trot, Cap'n Bill, and Button-Bright farewell.

l: the War of the Pinks and Blues, Sky Island
s: The War of the Pinks and Blues is listed as the title of chapter 19.

l: the amazing conquest of the Blues, Sky Island
s: Trot, supported by the Pinkies and aided by the billygoat, completes the conquest of the Blue Country, becoming Queen of the Blues; Ghip-Ghisizzle becomes Boolooroo and is ordered to rule kindly and avoid trouble.

l: the capture of Cap'n Bill, Sky Island
s: Cap'n Bill is captured after he pursues the retreating Blueskins alone and falls when his wooden leg steps into a hole. The Blueskins seize him, carry him into the Blue City, and bind him while the Pinkies are unable to reach him.

l: the tribulation of Trot, Sky Island
s: is_planned_by Six Snubnosed Princesses The Princesses punish Trot by shaking, slapping, pushing, and otherwise mistreating her after she refuses to act as their slave. Later they argue over harsher punishments, including beating her with knotted cords, locking her in a dark room, feeding her sand, or binding her to a windmill, but none of these proposed punishments occurs in this unit.

l: the Treasure Chamber, Sky Island
s: The Treasure Chamber is a dark, crowded, guarded room in the palace, holding the Boolooroo's accumulated riches, the Book of Records, and the Magic Umbrella. The Boolooroo keeps its key, Jimfred Jinksjones guards outside, and the Blue Wolf guards inside. Jimfred guards the entrance until Button-Bright deceives him into leaving; Button-Bright then unlocks and enters the chamber. Among gold, jewels, ornaments, cloths, furniture, vases, and bric-a-brac, he searches for the Magic Umbrella but does not find it.

l: the journey home, Sky Island
s: The journey home takes Trot, Cap'n Bill, and Button-Bright from Sky Island through the clouds and open sky to Earth. They encounter a Rainbow, stars, and a huge bird, eat food from the lunch basket, and land safely near Trot's house.

l: Dorothy, Sky Island
s: is_a friend [old, old] Dorothy is described as an old, old friend of Baum's readers. Readers compared Trot favorably to her, and Button-Bright previously had an adventure with Dorothy in Oz.

l: sky country, Sky Island
s: is_a fair land [remarkable] The sky country is described as a remarkable and fair land. Baum says that experiencing it makes him and the readers appreciate Mother Earth as a very good place to live.

l: Earth, Sky Island
s: Earth is a good place to live upon, beneath Sky Island, with ocean and mainland. It is home to Trot, Button-Bright, and Cap'n Bill when they are at home, and the intended destination of the strangers. Though the Boolooroo calls it an uninhabited, round, cold, barren ball of mud and water, the travelers contradict him. Unable to return without the Magic Umbrella, they eventually see Earth below, fly over its ocean, reach the mainland, and arrive at the high bluff near Trot's house.

l: readers, Sky Island
s: write_to L. Frank Baum [about how they like Sky Island] Baum's former readers approved of The Sea Fairies and wrote that they liked Trot almost as well as Dorothy. Their letters are Baum's greatest treasures, and he invites them to write and tell him how they like Sky Island.

l: Mrs. Griffith, Sky Island
s: Mrs. Griffith, Trot’s mother, lives in a frame cottage and is motherly and good, welcoming and feeding Button-Bright while often scolding Cap’n Bill and Trot.

l: Trot's house, Sky Island
s: Trot's house, home of Trot and Cap'n Bill, is a white cottage near a giant acacia on a high bluff, with a shed. Trot breakfasts there before flying, returns from town by Magic Umbrella, and comes home at dusk to find her mother cooking.

l: Pacific Ocean, Sky Island
s: The Pacific Ocean is the world's biggest lot of water, beyond the high bluff near Trot's house, with Sky Island on its horizon. Trot and Button-Bright meet beside it; later three voyagers fly over it toward Sky Island.

l: Philadelphia, Sky Island
s: Philadelphia is a big city and Button-Bright's distant home, at the other end of America from Trot's home; he lives there and finds an old umbrella that carries him toward Germantown.

l: the town, Sky Island
s: A bay-shore fishing town with a store; the Magic Umbrella brings Trot and Button-Bright there, Trot trades yarn inside while Button-Bright draws a crowd outside.

l: a parachute descent, Sky Island
s: Trot and Cap'n Bill infer that Button-Bright came down from the sky using his umbrella like a parachute. Button-Bright confirms that this was how he arrived, but the unit does not explain how he first got into the air.

l: Button-Bright's journey from Philadelphia, Sky Island
s: Button-Bright reaches the Pacific coast from Philadelphia by parachute descent with an umbrella, denying common travel methods and promising a later explanation.

l: frame cottage (Mrs. Griffith's cottage), Sky Island
s: is_a frame cottage [neat, on a high bluff, a little back from the sea, and covered with green vines] The frame cottage stands on a high bluff a little back from the sea and is covered with pretty green vines. It provides Button-Bright with food, shelter, and a place to stay overnight.

l: Magic, Sky Island
s: Magic is a lost art from before the characters’ births, associated with the Dark Ages; Button-Bright believes his flying umbrella proves it still exists, leading Cap’n Bill to reconsider.

l: fairies, Sky Island
s: Rosalie the Witch believes fairies, powerful and living in Pink Country, enchant the Magic Umbrella and defend Earth people from Pinkies’ injury.

l: flight of the Magic Umbrella, Sky Island
s: The flight of the Magic Umbrella is a swift, unfaltering air journey triggered when Button-Bright holds the umbrella open and speaks a destination or wishes to travel. It carries Button-Bright, Cap'n Bill, and Trot faster than railroad trains, amazing villagers because it flies without visible power. On a trial trip it passes over Smuggler's Cove, circles, and returns without stopping for a drifting boat. Later it crosses the Pacific toward Sky Island, through clouds and down in an arching descent.

l: swing seat, Sky Island
s: A seat suspended by six ropes: Cap'n Bill makes a broad board for Trot and Button-Bright, adds a second seat for himself, and all three ride safely in a trial flight.

l: flight from Sky Island to Earth, Sky Island
s: The air-ride is an exhilarating journey using the Magic Umbrella. It carries Trot, Button-Bright, and Cap'n Bill quickly and comfortably; Cap'n Bill overcomes his fear during a trial ride. The flight home begins at Sky Island, passes clouds and Polychrome, and gently lands on a bluff near Trot's house on Earth.

l: picnic, Sky Island
s: takes_place_at Sky Island [planned destination] Trot proposes a picnic on Sky Island because it is too far to reach by sailing or rowing. She packs a basket of food, which Cap'n Bill fastens beneath his seat for the journey.

l: the island, Sky Island
s: The island, whose right name is too hard to say, contains the Pink Country. As travelers approach, it grows larger, but the Magic Umbrella passes over it; later it shrinks behind them. Its rain-accustomed inhabitants and the Pinkies threaten strangers from its edge.

l: clouds, Sky Island
s: Clouds are vaporous, changeable formations that can appear as ships, trees, castles, palaces, dragons, and giants; travelers pass through black rain and white misty clouds before reaching clear blue sky.

l: the landing on Sky Island, Sky Island
s: The landing on Sky Island is a sudden, rough arrival: the basket thuds, Cap'n Bill lands forcefully, Trot and Button-Bright fall on him, and an angry voice protests.

l: the Blueskins, Sky Island
s: The Blueskins are a people and citizens of the Blue Country, especially the Blue City, and inhabitants of Sky Island. Blue-skinned, tall, lanky, large compared with the Pinkies, and described as ugly and fierce, they have egg-shaped heads, long thin necks, short round bodies, and exceptionally long legs. They wear blue silk liveries as palace servants and use long winding-up cords weighted at the ends as weapons. Every man and woman is a voter under the government of Sky Island. Each is allowed exactly six hundred years of life; at that term's end they pass away rather than die and enter the Great Blue Grotto. Jealous of strangers and possible royal favor, the Blueskins dislike, threaten, and often pursue unfamiliar visitors, including Trot, Cap'n Bill, and Button-Bright. They particularly hate the Six Snubnosed Princesses and are the Pinkies' natural enemies. They fear the Fog Bank above all else: no Blueskin has entered it, and pursuers stop when the travelers reach it. Their conflict with the Pinkies includes capturing prisoners in weighted cords, patching captured Pinkies, defending the City, and fighting with their cords, although several flee toward the Blue City when the Pinkies arrive. Many resent the Boolooroo, believing his treatment of the Earth people brought on the invasion. During the events, Blueskin soldiers capture the prisoners, carry out the Boolooroo's orders, chase escaping travelers, and later recapture Cap'n Bill. After Trot's conquest and the Boolooroo's defeat, they rejoice that the war is over, welcome Trot and the Pinkies, celebrate the destruction of the Great Knife, and receive Ghip-Ghisizzle as their new Boolooroo. Trot orders them to stop quarreling with the Pinkies and welcome them to the Blue City; she is also identified as their queen. Under Ghip-Ghisizzle after the conquest, they are secretly glad when Trot, the Pinkies, and the other strangers depart, and remain sullen during the departure.

l: the Royal Palace, Sky Island
s: The Royal Palace is a magnificent blue palace in Blue City, on Sky Island: the Boolooroo's royal residence and a building of six hundred tall towers and turrets, lofty rooms, broad corridors, passages, and superb blue furnishings. It contains royal apartments, servants' quarters and hall, the Royal Treasure Chamber, the Room of the Great Knife, prisoners' rooms, and areas for former Princesses. Richly blue-clad servants and guards at its entrance serve and protect it. For the strangers, it is safer than the City because servants and soldiers fear harming prisoners without the Boolooroo's permission. Trot is dragged there while Cap'n Bill and Button-Bright are assigned to servants' quarters; Button-Bright later steals the Treasure Chamber key and reaches the chamber. After an alarm fills it with guards, soldiers, and servants, Button-Bright, Cap'n Bill, and Trot escape through a little door. Trot returns at night, finds Cap'n Bill's hidden prison location, and Ghip-Ghisizzle escapes. Following the conquest, the palace hosts a feast and ball, its treasure and authority pass to Ghip-Ghisizzle, and the Boolooroo's family is expelled. A search there fails to find the Magic Umbrella, later said to have been discarded behind it.

l: the travelers' journey to Sky Island, Sky Island
s: Cap'n Bill, Trot, and Button-Bright travel by Magic Umbrella to Sky Island, but after lunch, blue cords prevent their attempted journey home.

l: the capture of Trot, Button-Bright, and Cap'n Bill, Sky Island
s: The Blueskins capture Cap'n Bill, Trot, and Button-Bright in a garden, creeping behind their bench and throwing thin, weighted blue cords around them and the Magic Umbrella. The cords pin each traveler's arms to their sides, leaving the three prisoners helpless under the Boolooroo and his people. After arranging for the Magic Umbrella to be secured, the Boolooroo releases them.

l: Indigo, Sky Island
s: Princess Indigo, one of the Six Snubnosed Princesses and the Boolooroo’s daughter, owns a blue dog. She declares Trot a slave and mistreats her, but Trot’s pets drive Indigo away; rescued by her sisters, she avoids her room because Trot is inside.

l: royal nectar, Sky Island
s: is_mixed_by Tiggle [in the royal pantry] Royal nectar is a drink for which the Boolooroo is very particular. Cap'n Bill is assigned to carry it, while Ghip-Ghisizzle arranges for Tiggle to mix it so that it will suit the Boolooroo and the royal household.

l: the prisoners, Sky Island
s: Trot, Button-Bright, and Cap'n Bill are captured, released because escape seems impossible without the Magic Umbrella, then condemned, threatened with patching, and assigned separate slavery.

l: enslavement, Sky Island
s: The Boolooroo declares Trot, Button-Bright, and Cap'n Bill slaves, assigning Trot to the Six Snubnosed Princesses, Cap'n Bill as Royal Nectar Mixer, and Button-Bright as Royal Bootblue.

l: patching, Sky Island
s: Patching is the Boolooroo’s severe punishment in Sky Island and the Blue Country. Using the Great Knife or slicing machine, prisoners are cut in two and mismatched halves are joined, causing the resulting person to lose individuality and potentially have conflicting desires. The Boolooroo threatens Ghip-Ghisizzle, guards, and strangers with patching, including a proposed head-rearranging variant. Ghip-Ghisizzle is to be joined with Tiggle but is rescued before it happens. After his escape, Cap’n Bill is scheduled for patching with Tiggle, and later the Boolooroo plans to join him to the billygoat. Trot prevents these punishments, turns the threat back on the Boolooroo, and finally forbids any further patching, choosing exile and loss of status instead.

l: Jimfred Jonesjinks, Sky Island
s: Jimfred Jonesjinks is a patched Blueskin and patched man, one half of a mismatched paired body with Fredjim Jinksjones. Joined from two people’s halves, he has mismatched features and a limp, guards the palace entrance, and is more intelligent than Fredjim. He says patching destroys individuality while Fredjim guards the Treasure Chamber.

l: Tiggle, Sky Island
s: Tiggle is a servant and prisoner of the Boolooroo who works in the royal pantry mixing royal nectar. Bound captive in the Room of the Great Knife, he is meant to be patched to Cap'n Bill, but Ghip-Ghisizzle replaces him and Trot frees him. Tiggle hides in a cellar of a deserted house to evade the Boolooroo's soldiers. A former servant of the former Boolooroo, he later returns after hearing the new Boolooroo wants him and recalls discarding the Magic Umbrella behind the palace.

l: Earth people, Sky Island
s: The Earth travelers, wearing Boolooroo uniforms, are enslaved by Blueskins in Blue Country but escape through the Fog Bank. In Pink Country, Pinkies capture them as suspected enemies. After they tell the truth about their adventures, Tourmaline and the Counselors judge them; despite support for honoring them, the order is to throw them into the sky.

l: Earth people, Sky Island
s: Earth people are strangers in the Pink Country: Trot, Button-Bright, and Cap'n Bill, whose truth Rosalie confirms before concluding fairies protect them unknowingly.

l: Royal Record Book, Sky Island
s: The Royal Record Book is a small light-blue leather book kept locked in the Treasure Chamber by the Boolooroo. It records the Pink Country as the Sunset Country and contains the terms of the Boolooroo’s rule and Ghip-Ghisizzle’s lawful succession. The Boolooroo hides it because it proves his permitted reign has expired. When it goes missing, he fears exposure. Button-Bright has taken it; Ghip-Ghisizzle reads it, learns the reign ended on Thursday, and recovers evidence that establishes his succession.

l: the Boolooroo's reign, Sky Island
s: The Boolooroo's reign is supposed to last three hundred years, but Ghip-Ghisizzle suspects that the current Boolooroo has already ruled for three hundred years and claims it has lasted only two hundred. If so, the Boolooroo is five hundred years old and is trying to gain another hundred years of rule.

l: royal bootblue duty, Sky Island
s: is_a high official position [in Sky Island] Royal bootblue duty requires Button-Bright to apply a finely perfumed blue paste to the royal boots and shoes and shine them. It is considered a high official position in Sky Island, and he is expected to perform it in the evening or early morning.

l: the Blue Country, Sky Island
s: The Blue Country is the blue half of Sky Island, beyond the Fog Bank. It has no sun, but moonlight every night; its fields are blue, and it contains Blue City, a mountain, the Great Blue Grotto, the Arch of Phinis, and plentiful blue goats. It is inhabited by nervous, restless Blueskins and is less delightful and less comfortable than the Pink Country. For three hundred years it was ruled by Boolooroo, whose cruel treatment of Earth people helped bring the Pinkies through the Fog Bank to threaten and conquer the country. Earlier, travelers were enslaved after Boolooroo stole their Magic Umbrella, but escaped through the Fog Bank; they also could not remain because the people hated them. After Trot and Cap'n Bill overpower Boolooroo, Trot takes the Blue Country into her kingdom, appoints Cap'n Bill Royal Manager, removes the former ruling family, and appoints Ghip-Ghisizzle Boolooroo. She plans peace with the Pinkies and a celebration in Blue City.

l: the Great Blue Grotto, Sky Island
s: The Great Blue Grotto is a fatal place at the foot of the mountain in the Blue Country, beyond the Arch of Phinis outside the City gates. When Blueskins' six hundred years end, they march into it and never return; the Boolooroo expects it to destroy three strangers sent there.
